fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/run -run TestPastLanding shows the method true for a run that visited land or merge and false for one that visited neither; go test -trimpath ./internal/daemon -run TestResumableOnlyAcceptedOrLandedPastLand shows an interrupted run on a landed change set that visited merge but not land picked, and one that visited neither skipped; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestRunResumeLandedPastMerge shows rhiza run resume accepting such a run and still refusing a landed run that visited neither; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/inbox-landed-resumable passes with a fixture run that visited merge but not land listed and not skipped. Touches internal/run/journal.go, internal/run/journal_test.go, internal/api/run.go, internal/api/run_test.go, internal/daemon/pick.go, internal/daemon/pick_test.go, internal/api/inbox.go and cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/inbox-landed-resumable.txtar.
fields.statement: A non-plan run on a landed change set counts as past its landing when it entered a land step or a merge step, not only a land step, so a conductor-default run (which lands on the branch and has no land step) interrupted after its merge (main's CI, close-out, ship, deploy-check) is resumable: rhiza run resume lets it through instead of refusing it as no longer accepted, the daemon's resumable pick takes it, and the inbox lists it instead of leaving it out as gone. One run.State method decides it for all three; a landed run that entered neither stays refused, skipped and gone as today.
